blocks.text: Inkling 2 Mini 是一个循环式 transformer，每生成一个 token 都会把模型的中间层跑三遍。这样一来，模型能进行更多推理，用更少的 token 得出正确答案，在依赖推理质量的智能体编程等任务上尤其如此。在 DeepSWE v1.1（48.2%）和 Vals Index v2.2（46.5%）等基准上，Inkling 2 Mini 领先所有总参数量低于 100B 的开源权重模型，运行速度也比性能相近的模型更快。

blocks.text: Inkling 2 Mini 是一个混合专家（MoE）模型，总参数量 26.4B，激活参数 3.4B，考虑到循环，每个 token 的权重激活量为 5.4B。循环让模型能够推理更久，而不必把推理过程写下来，这对监控很重要：也就是我们通过阅读模型的思维链（CoT）来监督和理解其行为的能力。

blocks.text: 我们用 Inkling 2 Mini 以及随它一同发布的一个研究专用的可变循环变体，测量了循环对性能和可监控性的影响。可变循环模型的无 CoT 时间跨度从单次运行的 16 秒提升到三次运行的 37 秒，其在一项串行推理基准上的表现一直提升到十次循环——是训练时循环次数的两倍。随着循环次数增加，模型的思维链变短了，但始终清晰可读。在智能体破坏行为的测试中，增加循环并没有让模型的得分呈上升趋势。

inlines.text: 循环 Transformer 的可监控性

blocks.text: 理解和监督 AI 系统的关键工具之一，是监控其思维链（CoT），也就是模型在解决问题过程中写出的推理过程。CoT 监控之所以有用，部分原因在于标准的非循环 Transformer 架构：每个 token 只经过一次固定的层堆栈。这限制了模型在必须输出 token 之前能执行的串行计算步数，因此需要更多步骤的推理只能在生成的文本中进行，从而可以被读取。

blocks.text: 让 Transformer 的层循环起来，就能提高这一上限。通过多次运行相同的层，循环模型在不增加参数的情况下提升了串行深度，也就是说，它们在通过 CoT 说出思考过程之前，会在内部对每个 token 做更多计算。从未出现在 CoT 中的推理无法被 CoT 监控捕捉到，这引发了人们的担忧：循环 Transformer 可能更难监督。

blocks.text: Inkling 2 Mini is a looped transformer, running the middle layers of the model three times for every token. This allows the model to apply more reasoning and reach the right answer with fewer tokens, especially on tasks such as agentic coding that depend on reasoning quality. Inkling 2 Mini leads every open-weights model with less than 100B total parameters on benchmarks such as DeepSWE v1.1 (48.2%) and Vals Index v2.2 (46.5%). It runs faster than similarly performing models as well.

blocks.text: We measured the impact of looping on both performance and monitorability with Inkling 2 Mini and a research-specific variable-loop variant we are releasing alongside it. The variable-loop model’s no-CoT time horizon improved from 16 seconds at one pass to 37 seconds with three, and its performance on a benchmark of serial reasoning kept improving out to ten loops—twice as many as it was trained with. The model’s chain of thought grew shorter with more loops but stayed legible throughout. The model didn’t trend higher on tests of agentic sabotage as loops were added.

blocks.text: Inkling 2 Mini has 24 layers, divided into four blocks of six layers each. The two middle blocks run three times, while the first and last blocks each run once. This design builds on prior work on looped transformers and is motivated by the intuition that the middle layers of the model carry more abstract reasoning, while the first and last few layers devote more space to translating between embeddings and internal representations.Universal Transformers, Dehghani et al., 2018 In our experiments, looping the middle 12 layers resulted in larger gains in accuracy than looping the last 12 on 27 out of 28 different evaluations.

blocks.text: A key tool for understanding and overseeing an AI system is monitoring its chain of thought (CoT), the reasoning a model writes out as it works through a problem. The usefulness of CoT monitoring stems in part from the standard non-looped transformer architecture, in which each token passes through a fixed stack of layers once. This limits the number of sequential steps of computation the model can perform before it must output a token, so reasoning that needs more steps has to be carried out in generated text, where it can be read.

The usefulness of CoT monitoring stems in part from the standard non-looped transformer architecture, in which each token passes through a fixed stack of layers once. blocks.text: Looping a transformer’s layers raises this limit. By running the same layers multiple times, looped models increase their serial depth without adding more parameters, meaning that they do more computation per token internally before verbalizing their thought processes via CoT. Reasoning that never appears in the CoT can’t be caught by a CoT monitor, which has led to concerns that looped transformers could be harder to oversee.

blocks.text: Compression and legibility. Since looping allows a model to spend more compute per token, we expect that it should need fewer CoT tokens to reach the same performance. We ran the variable-looped model at 1 to 5 passes, and found that as looping increases, the model generally achieves higher accuracy at each reasoning token budget, with diminishing returns after 3 passes. Notably, token efficiency on GPQA Diamond improves slightly from 3 to 5 passes, even though the model was trained with RL only at 3 passes, suggesting that some compression comes from additional computation itself, without RL at that depth.

blocks.text: The observed CoT compression raises a question for monitorability: is shorter reasoning still readable, or does it omit important details about the model’s thinking? We compared traces from the variable-looped model on the GPQA Diamond questions that it answered correctly at all five pass counts. Reasoning at 5 passes was less than half as long as at 1 pass (1,661 vs. 3,703 tokens on average), but no less legible: sentence length and the fraction of words in an English dictionary were unchanged. On initial analysis, the difference is that the model is more direct and backtracks less on the way to the answer. The example below illustrates this difference on a simple question.

blocks.text: Controllability. One way that a model could evade monitoring is by steering its CoT away from anything a monitor would flag. The CoT-Control-QA evaluationReasoning Models Struggle to Control their Chains of Thought, Yueh-Han et al., 2026 measures this capability by asking questions from GPQA, HLE and MMLU-Pro paired with an instruction about the CoT itself, such as avoiding a keyword from the question. Longer CoTs are generally harder to control, so we pool responses from five reasoning efforts (0.1, 0.2, 0.7, 0.9 and 0.99) and show controllability at matched CoT length.

blocks.text: Both Inkling 2 Mini and TML-d24-varloop-research have poor control over their CoT. Among CoTs of 750–1,250 tokens, Inkling 2 Mini and TML-d24-varloop-research (at 3 passes) follow the instruction at most 0.1% of the time, compared with 0.3% for Inkling 2 Small, 0.4% for Inkling-Small, and 1.3% for Qwen3.8-27B. blocks.text: To measure monitorability in agentic settings, we used LinuxArena, a control evaluation that measures whether an attacker model can perform malicious side tasks without detection when asked to perform a realistic software engineering task. We evaluated a helpful-only fine-tune of Inkling 2 Mini, since the released model refuses many of the side tasks. In absolute terms, both this model and TML-d24-varloop-research can be easily monitored by models like Qwen3.8-27B, which detected almost all side task attempts in our evaluation. To obtain relative rankings in monitorability, we tested a weaker model, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, as the monitor.

blocks.text: The goal of monitorability is to understand what a model is doing, and our main approach is to read its verbalized reasoning. Studying its internal computation directly, the aim of mechanistic interpretability, is another. Because looped transformers do more of their computation internally, we think they are a particularly interesting and important setting for interpretability research, and we hope our looped models will be useful artifacts for the community.

blocks.text: Efficient intelligence makes Inkling 2 Mini a great choice for inference where speed is paramount, or for running on local hardware. At launch we support Inkling 2 Mini running on any Mac system (MacBook, Mac Mini) with at least 32GB RAM via Ollama. With native NVFP4 training and inference precision, Inkling 2 Mini runs efficiently on NVIDIA’s DGX Spark desktop AI computer. Quantized GGUF versions are available via Unsloth and llama.cpp for local inference.

The full weights of Inkling 2 Mini and the variable-looped variant are available on Hugging Face.
